explanation: In the C++ object model, virtual functions are implemented via a vtable (virtual table), which is a per-class static table of function pointers. Each polymorphic object contains an implicit pointer to its class's vtable, enabling dynamic dispatch at runtime. This mechanism allows C++ to resolve function calls to the most derived override during execution, supporting runtime polymorphism. Understanding the internal layout of vtables, how they are constructed, and how objects reference them is crucial for grasping the low-level behavior of virtual functions and their impact on memory layout and performance.
